Changeset in the root `.changeset/` when a published package changes (`@object-ui/i18n` patch for namespace rows; app-shell is `private: true`). ⛔ `ui/.github/**` and the root `ci.yml` are out of bounds. Shared files: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/appReportIndex.ts`, `AppReportIndexView.tsx`, `chrome/CommandPalette.tsx` and `hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts` are in no open PR on `origin/main` `4daad78f` (measured over all 27 open PRs' file lists). `useNavMemberGates.ts` is read by the sidebar, the landing and the palette: ⛔ change no existing export's behaviour there; add, don't alter.

### Ruling (cannot be re-ruled)

None on the card: triage 2026-10-27 21:06Z confirmed p3 only. No maintainer ruling.

### PM mechanism assumptions (measure; disproof welcome)

On `origin/main` `4daad78f`:
- `useAppReportEntries` (`views/appReportIndex.ts` ≈L208) lists `appShippedReports` (the app package's own reports ∪ every report a `type: 'report'` entry names) filtered only by `mayOpenReport` (object-read on each dataset's object). It never asks the navigation's member gates (`visible`, `requiredPermissions`, capabilities) that `useNavMemberGates` / `navEntriesShownToMember` (`hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts` ≈L312/≈L411) give the sidebar. HotCRM's reports are package-owned, so a report the nav hides (`visible: OPPORTUNITY_AUDIENCE`) still lists through the owner rule.
- The ⌘K palette (`chrome/CommandPalette.tsx` ≈L232) adds `useAppReportEntries` minus the report names in its own `navItems`. Measure whether `navItems` is already gated: if it is, a report whose nav entry the member cannot see drops out of `navReportNames` and comes back through `appReports`, the same leak through a second door. The fix covers both consumers through the one module.
- The likely rule: a report that one or more navigation entries name is listed only when at least one of those entries is shown to the member; a report no entry names keeps today's rule (objectui#13020 gave those their only door; don't take it away). Measure it against the card's three personas and say in the PR body which rule you kept and why. Pending nav data reads (an entry's API `dataSource`) count as not shown, as the sidebar treats them.

### Scope

File surface: `views/appReportIndex.ts` (the gate), `AppReportIndexView.tsx` / `CommandPalette.tsx` only if the hook's signature has to change, `hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts` only for an additive helper, tests. Tests: an app whose package owns reports A, B, C, where nav entry for C has `visible: false` (and one with `requiredPermissions` the member lacks): the index and the palette list A and B, not C; a member for whom C's entry is visible lists all three; a report no nav entry names still lists. Ablation: drop the gate and the hidden-entry test turns red.

### Tier

No path-derived mandate. `TIER_DEFAULT`, effort `medium` (S–M). `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` expected. `@object-ui/app-shell` is `private: true`: `skip-changeset` unless you touch a published package.

## Order amendment · `domain:ui#5` · `session_01JQwxbXGpVJHZTXXerMoY4C` · 2026-10-28T02:03Z

Amends dispatch order 6458600854 and Claim 6458625748 (file surface), on the card thread's measurement against `origin/main` `acc9c57d`.

- The ⌘K palette's `navItems` is `flattenNavigation(nav)` filtered by each leaf's own `visible` only. It skips `requiredPermissions`, `requiresObject` / `requiresService`, and an ancestor group's `visible` (the flatten drops groups). A report entry hidden that way stays in the palette's nav door (`reportItems`), so gating `appReportIndex.ts` alone cannot meet the order's palette test.
- **Surface widened:** `ui/packages/app-shell/src/chrome/CommandPalette.tsx` may change its `navItems` to `flattenNavigation(navEntriesShownToMember(nav, gates))` with `gates = useNavMemberGates()`, the sidebar's own gates, in its own commit. That also gates the palette's object, dashboard and page entries and its record-search scope as the sidebar does; name that in the PR body.
- Conditions: ⛔ no change to any existing export of `hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts`; no second fetch (the entry `dataSource` reads go through the same reader the sidebar uses: show it in a test or by citation); an entry whose read is pending stays hidden in the palette as in the sidebar. Tests add: a report entry with `requiredPermissions` the member lacks, and one inside a `visible: false` group, are absent from both palette doors and from the index.
